pr_semantic_analysis.change_summary: The change introduces a browser service worker that intercepts image asset GETs, serves successful responses from a deployment-versioned cache, supports background preloading, and allows component teardown to cancel pending image fetches. It also adds a production Compose shutdown target. The supplied diff does not show service-worker registration, so whether these mechanisms affect a real installation cannot be established here.

behavior_changes.description: When the service worker controls a client, matching original and thumbnail asset GETs are handled cache-first; successful network responses are stored and later requests for the same URL can be returned from browser cache.
evidence: The fetch handler selects asset original/thumbnail paths and delegates their responses to immichAsset.
immichAsset checks Cache Storage before fetching and stores HTTP 200 responses.

citations.quoted_text: let response = useCache ? await cache.match(url) : undefined;

behavior_changes.description: Photo-viewer preloading now asks the service worker to fetch and cache adjacent image URLs rather than creating browser Image objects directly.
evidence: The photo viewer sends each eligible preload URL through preloadImageUrl.
The service worker handles preload messages by invoking its asset-loading path.

behavior_changes.description: When an image thumbnail or viewer image is torn down, it can notify the service worker to abort a pending fetch for that URL, reducing work for images no longer needed.
evidence: Thumbnail teardown posts a cancellation for its URL.
The service worker looks up the URL's pending AbortController and aborts it.

behavior_changes.description: Activating a new service-worker version claims existing clients and removes every Cache Storage entry whose name is not the current deployment cache name.
evidence: Activation runs cache cleanup.
Cleanup enumerates all cache names and deletes names other than CACHE.

behavior_changes.description: Developers can now stop and remove the production Docker Compose stack and its orphaned containers through the new prod-down Make target.
evidence: The target invokes docker compose down using the production Compose file.

important_symbols.reason: This is the central cache/network path for intercepted and preloaded assets; it defines cache lookup, fetch cancellation, response validation, and cache population.
Its message handler connects component lifecycle events to service-worker preload and cancellation behavior.
It controls deployment-time cache cleanup and currently operates across all Cache Storage names visible to the origin.

It replaces direct image-object preloading with service-worker-directed caching.

local_risks.description: If asset responses are authorization-dependent while their URLs remain the same across users, caching and matching only by URL can return an image stored under a previous session to a later session. This would be a material cross-user data exposure unless another layer guarantees URL-level isolation or clears the cache on identity changes.

local_risks.description: Cancellation ownership is global per URL rather than per component or request. If multiple consumers load the same URL, a teardown from one consumer can abort the controller currently stored for another consumer; overlapping loads also overwrite each other's map entries.

Activation cleanup deletes every origin cache other than the current service-worker cache. If any unrelated feature owns a differently named cache, an update will remove that feature's cached state as well.

Cache population is started without awaiting its promise. A service-worker lifecycle termination or rejected cache write can therefore leave the request successful but the intended preload/cache entry unavailable.
